<a id="boundedtracequeue-1"></a>

## `BoundedTraceQueue<T>`

sealed class · `` CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.BoundedTraceQueue`1 `` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A hand-off queue between the game threads and the single writer thread: unbounded in the BCL, bounded here by an interlocked counter so a burst can never eat memory.

Overflow drops the newest item rather than blocking. A game thread waiting on a log is the one outcome worse than a missing line, and the drop count is reported in the health snapshot and the footer so a truncated trace is never silent.

<a id="boundedtracequeue-1--ctor"></a>

**Parameters**

- `capacity`: Maximum items held. Values below 1 are treated as 1.

### `long Dropped { get; }`

Items dropped because the queue was full.

Forgets everything queued. Only used when shutting down or by tests.

<a id="boundedtracequeue-1--trydequeue"></a>

<a id="boundedtracequeue-1--tryenqueue"></a>

<a id="bufferedfiletracewriter"></a>

## `BufferedFileTraceWriter`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.BufferedFileTraceWriter` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Implements: `IDisposable`, [`ITraceWriter`](#itracewriter)

Buffers trace lines in memory, writes them out in blocks, and rolls over to a new part once the current file gets too large. A trace at full level produces thousands of lines a second; one file write per line would cost more frame time than the Harmony prefixes themselves. Every member is guarded by one lock, because calls arrive from whichever thread the game happened to be on.

<a id="bufferedfiletracewriter--ctor"></a>

### `BufferedFileTraceWriter(string path, int flushThresholdBytes = 65536, long maxBytesPerFile = 0)`

Opens (and truncates) the first part of the trace file, creating its directory if needed.

**Parameters**

- `path`: Full path of the .jsonl file; later parts get a `-partN` suffix.
- `flushThresholdBytes`: Bytes to buffer before flushing. Values below 1 flush every line.
- `maxBytesPerFile`: Bytes per part before rolling over. 0 or less never rotates.

Bytes buffered before an automatic flush.

<a id="clickdedupe"></a>

## `ClickDedupe`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.ClickDedupe` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Collapses the duplicate click lines the input postfix produces.

`InputController.GetClickDown` is polled by more than one caller per frame, and every caller that sees it return true reaches the postfix, so one physical click wrote two `Input.click` lines. The truth is "one click per frame at one position", which is what this keeps.

Pure, so the rule is tested rather than observed in a log.

<a id="clickdedupe--noframe"></a>

### `const int NoFrame = -2147483648`

Frame number that means "nothing accepted yet".

<a id="clickdedupe--reset"></a>

### `void Reset()`

Forgets the last accepted click.

<a id="clickdedupe--shouldwrite"></a>

### `bool ShouldWrite(int frame, float x, float y)`

Whether this click should be written.

**Parameters**

- `frame`: Unity's frame counter.
- `x`: Cursor x in pixels; rounded to whole pixels before comparing.
- `y`: Cursor y in pixels; rounded to whole pixels before comparing.

**Returns:** False when the same frame already wrote a click at the same whole-pixel position; true otherwise. A second click at a different position in the same frame is written, because that is a different event, not a duplicate report of one.

<a id="curatedevents"></a>

## `CuratedEvents`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.CuratedEvents` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The short list of calls that are interesting enough to mirror to the BepInEx console at Info, and the only calls patched at [`TraceLevel.Events`](#tracelevel--events). Curated calls also get a postfix so their return value is recorded; nothing else does.

Names verified against game v1.17.2. Two names from the original list do not exist in this build — `PomodoroService.StartPomodoroTimer` (the real entry point is `StartPomodoro`) and `MusicManager.Play` only exists as an `AudioClip` overload. They are kept in the table anyway: an unmatched entry costs nothing and the list keeps working if a future game version renames things back.

<a id="focuswindow"></a>

## `FocusWindow`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.FocusWindow` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Remembers whether the game window has focus and when that last changed, so a frame-time spike can be attributed to the user alt-tabbing instead of reported as a stutter.

The game lowers its own frame rate while it is in the background (verified by the user), and macOS stalls the process across a space switch. Both produce 250 ms+ frames and a low average fps that have nothing to do with the mod. A reading this type attributes is still written to the trace file, tagged `unfocused`, but never mirrored to the console.

Pure and clock-agnostic: the caller passes `Time.realtimeSinceStartup`.

<a id="focuswindow--attributionseconds"></a>

### `const double AttributionSeconds = 2.0`

Seconds after a focus change during which a reading is still blamed on it. Covers the frame focus was lost on and the reload cost on the way back in.

<a id="focuswindow--focuschangecause"></a>

### `const string FocusChangeCause = "focus-change"`

[`FocusWindow.CauseAt`](#focuswindow--causeat) when the stall is the focus change itself.

<a id="focuswindow--holdseconds"></a>

### `const double HoldSeconds = 0.75`

How long a health event waits before it is attributed and emitted.

<a id="focuswindow--nearchangeseconds"></a>

### `const double NearChangeSeconds = 0.75`

How far either side of a focus change a stall is taken to BE that change.

Measured, not guessed: in the 17:41 session every ~1.1 s spike was followed within 20 ms by `focusChanged(false)`. Unity raises the callback after the stall it caused, so a spike emitted the instant it is measured always reads as focused. Health events are therefore held for [`FocusWindow.HoldSeconds`](#focuswindow--holdseconds) and attributed once the callback has had its chance to arrive.

<a id="focuswindow--unfocusedcause"></a>

### `const string UnfocusedCause = "unfocused"`

[`FocusWindow.CauseAt`](#focuswindow--causeat) when the window is in the background, or just came back.

<a id="focuswindow--focused"></a>

### `bool Focused { get; }`

Whether the window currently has focus, as last reported.

<a id="focuswindow--attributes"></a>

### `bool Attributes(double nowSeconds)`

True when a bad reading taken at `nowSeconds` should be blamed on the window: either it has no focus right now, or focus changed within [`FocusWindow.AttributionSeconds`](#focuswindow--attributionseconds) - which covers the seconds after a regain, where the game is still catching up.

**Parameters**

- `nowSeconds`: Now, in seconds since start-up.

<a id="focuswindow--causeat"></a>

### `string CauseAt(double eventAtSeconds, double nowSeconds)`

Why a reading taken at `eventAtSeconds` and attributed at `nowSeconds` is the window's fault, or null when it is not.

**Parameters**

- `eventAtSeconds`: When the reading was taken, in seconds since start-up.
- `nowSeconds`: When it is being attributed - normally [`FocusWindow.HoldSeconds`](#focuswindow--holdseconds) later, by which time Unity's focus callback has arrived.

**Returns:** [`FocusWindow.FocusChangeCause`](#focuswindow--focuschangecause) when the stall is the switch itself, [`FocusWindow.UnfocusedCause`](#focuswindow--unfocusedcause) when the window is in the background or just came back, null when the game is simply running badly and someone should look at it.

<a id="focuswindow--change"></a>

### `void Change(bool focused, double atSeconds)`

Records a focus change. Called from `Application.focusChanged`; a repeat of the state we already hold does not restart the window.

**Parameters**

- `focused`: The new focus state.
- `atSeconds`: When it changed, in seconds since start-up.

<a id="focuswindow--changednear"></a>

### `bool ChangedNear(double atSeconds, double windowSeconds)`

True when a focus change happened within `windowSeconds` either side of `atSeconds`.

**Parameters**

- `atSeconds`: When the reading was taken, in seconds since start-up.
- `windowSeconds`: Half-width of the window; negative is treated as zero.

<a id="healtheventhold"></a>

## `HealthEventHold`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.HealthEventHold` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Holds a health event for [`FocusWindow.HoldSeconds`](#focuswindow--holdseconds) before it is emitted, so it can be attributed with information that does not exist yet when it is measured.

Unity raises `focusChanged` *after* the stall the switch caused: in the 17:41 session every ~1.1 s spike was followed within 20 ms by `focused=false`. Emitting the spike the instant it is measured therefore always tagged it `unfocused=false` and mirrored it to the console - the exact noise the user asked to be rid of. Waiting a fraction of a second costs nothing and makes the tag true.

Pure and clock-agnostic; the caller passes `Time.realtimeSinceStartup`.

<a id="healtheventhold--capacity"></a>

### `const int Capacity = 64`

Events held at once before the oldest is dropped. A 250 ms spike threshold caps the real rate at about four a second, so three is the realistic depth; this is a bound against a pathological stall storm, not a working limit.

<a id="healtheventhold--count"></a>

### `int Count { get; }`

Events waiting to be released.

<a id="healtheventhold--dropped"></a>

### `long Dropped { get; }`

Events lost to [`HealthEventHold.Capacity`](#healtheventhold--capacity). Never silent: the caller reports it.

<a id="healtheventhold--hold"></a>

### `void Hold(string name, double atSeconds, params (string, object)[] fields)`

Holds one event.

**Parameters**

- `name`: Bus event name, e.g. `spike`.
- `atSeconds`: When the reading was taken, in seconds since start-up.
- `fields`: The payload as measured.

<a id="healtheventhold--release"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<HeldHealthEvent> Release(double nowSeconds)`

Every event whose hold has expired by `nowSeconds`, oldest first, in the order they were measured. Returns an empty list rather than null when none are due, so the per-frame caller allocates nothing in the common case.

**Parameters**

- `nowSeconds`: Now, in seconds since start-up.

<a id="healtheventhold--releaseall"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<HeldHealthEvent> ReleaseAll()`

Everything still held, released regardless of time. For shutdown.

## `HealthStats`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.HealthStats` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

<a id="ratelimiter"></a>

## `RateLimiter`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.RateLimiter` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A one-second token bucket per method key, with an adaptive downsample for polling methods.

The first 90-second run produced 61,444 lines, of which the great majority came from methods the game calls every frame on purpose — `GetCurrentMusicProgress`, `AudioPlayer.Stop` (883,406 suppressed calls on its own), input and cursor polling. A flat cap pins each of them at the cap forever, so the file is dominated by noise and the count of what was dropped is lost. A method that overruns the cap in three consecutive windows is therefore reclassified as polling and switched to one aggregate line per window carrying the exact call count and the last arguments seen; five quiet windows put it back. Nothing is lost, only merged.

**Parameters**

- `permitsPerSecond`: Lines written per key per second. 0 or less means no limit at all.
- `nowMilliseconds`: Monotonic clock in milliseconds. Defaults to `Environment.TickCount`.
- `pollingCapPerSecond`: Aggregate lines per second once a key is classified as polling.

<a id="ratelimiter--defaultpollingcappersecond"></a>

Default aggregate lines per second for a polling key.

<a id="ratelimiter--windowstoenterpolling"></a>

Consecutive over-cap windows before a key is treated as polling.

<a id="ratelimiter--windowstoleavepolling"></a>

### `const int WindowsToLeavePolling = 5`

Consecutive under-cap windows before a polling key goes back to normal.

<a id="ratelimiter--trackedkeys"></a>

<a id="satoneconsolelines"></a>

## `SatoneConsoleLines`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.SatoneConsoleLines` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The two console records that matter most to a person watching the log: what Satone said, and what she is doing.

These two events come from `CWYEvents`, whose payload is the event record's own `Fields()` - so unlike every other producer they cannot name their tag and field order at the emit site. They are built here instead, and [`ConsoleEventMap`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.md#consoleeventmap) routes to them.

The generic bus mirror used to show the first six payload members cut at 60 characters, which is right for a health reading and wrong for a sentence: the one line the user actually reads arrived truncated in the middle of the dialogue. The fixed layout below never drops a field, and caps only the sentence, at [`SatoneConsoleLines.TextLimit`](#satoneconsolelines--textlimit) characters per language.

<a id="traceadmission"></a>

## `TraceAdmission`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.TraceAdmission` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The per-method rate decision, made entirely with interlocked operations on the method's own [`TraceEntry`](#traceentry).

The previous version took one process-wide lock and did a string-keyed dictionary lookup per call. With `AudioPlayer.Stop` alone at roughly 13,000 calls a second and eighty more pollers behind it, that lock *was* the 55 % frame-time regression. Here the common case — a call inside an open window on a method already classified as polling — is one volatile read, one compare, one interlocked increment and one volatile write.

Window rollover is elected by a compare-and-swap on [`TraceEntry.WindowStartTicks`](#traceentry--windowstartticks): exactly one thread wins and does the bookkeeping, every other thread takes the ordinary path.

<a id="traceadmission--windowstoenterpolling"></a>

### `const int WindowsToEnterPolling = 3`

Consecutive over-cap windows before a method is treated as polling.

<a id="traceadmission--windowstoleavepolling"></a>

### `const int WindowsToLeavePolling = 5`

Consecutive under-cap windows before a polling method goes back to normal.

<a id="traceadmission--admit"></a>

### `static AdmitResult Admit(TraceEntry entry, long nowTicks, long windowTicks, long pollingWindowTicks, int permitsPerSecond)`

Takes one permit and says what to do with the call.

**Parameters**

- `entry`: The method's descriptor; its state is updated in place.
- `nowTicks`: A `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp()` reading.
- `windowTicks`: Length of a normal window, in stopwatch ticks.
- `pollingWindowTicks`: Length of an aggregate window, in stopwatch ticks.
- `permitsPerSecond`: Lines per window before suppression. 0 or less means no limit.

<a id="traceadmission--rememberargs"></a>

Stores the raw arguments of the call just seen, for the next aggregate line.

<a id="tracearchive"></a>

## `TraceArchive`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.TraceArchive` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Archives one trace part with gzip, archive-first: the original is deleted only after the archive has been flushed to disk, decompressed again, and matched on length and CRC-32.

Crash safety, step by step: the archive is written as `.gz.tmp` (a crash leaves the original plus a temp that the next run clears); the temp is renamed only once verified (a crash after that leaves the original plus a good archive, and the next run redoes the part); the original is removed last, and only if its size and timestamp are what was compressed.

<a id="tracearchive--buffersize"></a>

### `const int BufferSize = 81920`

Read/write buffer size.

<a id="tracearchive--compressandreplace"></a>

### `static TraceArchiveResult CompressAndReplace(string sourcePath, string archivePath, CancellationToken cancel)`

Compresses `sourcePath` to `archivePath`, verifies the archive, then deletes the source.

**Parameters**

- `sourcePath`: The plain part.
- `archivePath`: Where the archive goes; an existing file there is replaced once the new one verifies.
- `cancel`: Checked between buffers; a cancelled run removes its temp and keeps the original.

**Returns:** The sizes, and a note for anything non-fatal.

**Exceptions**

- `OperationCanceledException`: `cancel` fired; the original is intact.
- `InvalidDataException`: The archive did not verify; the original is intact.
- `IOException`: Reading, writing, or the final checks failed; the original is intact.

<a id="tracearchive--verify"></a>

### `static void Verify(string archivePath, long expectedBytes, uint expectedCrcState, CancellationToken cancel)`

Decompresses an archive to the end and checks its length and content checksum.

**Parameters**

- `archivePath`: The gzip file.
- `expectedBytes`: The original's length.
- `expectedCrcState`: The original's running CRC-32 state (not [`Crc32.Finish`](#crc32--finish)ed).
- `cancel`: Checked between buffers.

**Exceptions**

- `InvalidDataException`: Length or checksum differ, or the gzip stream is corrupt.
- `OperationCanceledException`: `cancel` fired.

<a id="traceclock"></a>

## `TraceClock`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.TraceClock` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Wall-clock time for trace lines, read from a cheap monotonic counter and put back on the system clock whenever the two part.

The trace stamps hundreds of lines a second, so the game thread only reads a counter (`Stopwatch.GetTimestamp`) and the writer thread turns that reading into a time from one pairing of counter and system time, the anchor. On macOS the counter stops while the machine sleeps: in one test trace game-method lines ran about 24 minutes behind the bus lines after a sleep. The counter also cannot see the system clock being set (by the user or NTP), nor a time-zone or daylight-saving change.

[`TraceClock.Check`](#traceclock--check) compares the counter's idea of "now" with the system clock. When they differ by more than [`TraceClock.Threshold`](#traceclock--threshold), or the UTC offset changed, it records a new anchor and returns a [`TraceClockJump`](#traceclockjump) for the caller to log. A reading keeps converting with the anchor that was current when it was taken (the newest [`TraceClock.AnchorHistory`](#traceclock--anchorhistory) anchors are kept), so a line queued before a sleep keeps its time even when it is written after the re-anchor. A reading taken after the machine woke but before the next check still uses the old anchor; [`TraceClock.Poll`](#traceclock--poll) keeps that window to [`TraceClock.PollInterval`](#traceclock--pollinterval).

Pure: the counter, its frequency and the system clock are injected, so tests drive all three. Thread-safe: conversions read an immutable anchor list without a lock; checks take a lock, so two threads that notice the same jump re-anchor once.

<a id="traceclock--ctor"></a>

### `TraceClock(Func<long> counter, long frequency, Func<DateTimeOffset> systemNow, TimeSpan? threshold = null, TimeSpan? pollInterval = null)`

Creates a clock anchored at the current counter reading and system time.

**Parameters**

- `counter`: A monotonic counter, e.g. `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp`.
- `frequency`: Counter units per second, e.g. `Stopwatch.Frequency`.
- `systemNow`: The system clock, e.g. `() => DateTimeOffset.Now`.
- `threshold`: Re-anchor above this difference; null uses [`TraceClock.DefaultThreshold`](#traceclock--defaultthreshold).
- `pollInterval`: Counter time between [`TraceClock.Poll`](#traceclock--poll) measurements; null uses [`TraceClock.DefaultPollInterval`](#traceclock--defaultpollinterval).

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `counter` or `systemNow` is null.
- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: `frequency` is not positive, or `threshold` or `pollInterval` is negative.

<a id="traceclock--anchorhistory"></a>

### `const int AnchorHistory = 8`

Anchors kept for readings taken before the latest re-anchor.

<a id="traceclock--defaultpollinterval"></a>

### `static readonly TimeSpan DefaultPollInterval`

How often [`TraceClock.Poll`](#traceclock--poll) measures, in counter time.

<a id="traceclock--defaultthreshold"></a>

### `static readonly TimeSpan DefaultThreshold`

Difference between the counter and the system clock above which the clock re-anchors.

<a id="traceclock--frequency"></a>

### `long Frequency { get; }`

Counter units per second.

<a id="traceclock--now"></a>

### `DateTimeOffset Now { get; }`

Now, from the counter and the current anchor. Never reads the system clock.

<a id="traceclock--pollinterval"></a>

### `TimeSpan PollInterval { get; }`

<a id="traceclock--reanchors"></a>

How many times the clock has re-anchored since it was created.

<a id="traceclock--threshold"></a>

### `TimeSpan Threshold { get; }`

<a id="traceclock--timestamp"></a>

<a id="traceclock--check"></a>

### `TraceClockJump Check(string reason)`

Measures the counter against the system clock now and re-anchors when they differ by more than [`TraceClock.Threshold`](#traceclock--threshold) or the system clock's UTC offset changed.

**Parameters**

**Returns:** The jump that was corrected, or null when the clock was still right.

<a id="traceclock--poll"></a>

### `TraceClockJump Poll(string reason)`

[`TraceClock.Check`](#traceclock--check), but only when at least [`TraceClock.PollInterval`](#traceclock--pollinterval) of counter time has passed since the last measurement. Cheap enough to call from a loop.

**Parameters**

- `reason`: What prompted the measurement, for the log.

**Returns:** The jump that was corrected, or null.

<a id="traceclock--towall"></a>

### `DateTimeOffset ToWall(long timestamp)`

The wall-clock time of a counter reading, using the newest anchor taken at or before it. A reading older than every kept anchor uses the oldest one.

**Parameters**

- `timestamp`: A reading of the same counter this clock was built with.

**Returns:** The wall-clock time, in the UTC offset of the anchor used.

The `sys` value used for classes in the root namespace.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--selfsystem"></a>

The `sys` value used for lines the trace writes about itself.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--uisystem"></a>

### `const string UiSystem = "ui"`

The `sys` value used for Unity user-interface events.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--bus"></a>

### `string Bus(DateTimeOffset when, int frame, double realtime, string gameClock, string system, string name, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object> payload, int threadId)`

One event published on `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Bus.TraceBus` by another plugin. The payload is flattened to top level so a reader can filter on its fields directly; a key that would collide with the line's own members is dropped rather than shadowing it.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--call"></a>

### `string Call(DateTimeOffset when, int frame, double realtime, string gameClock, string systemName, string className, string methodName, IReadOnlyList<string> args, int threadId, string instance, string returnValue = null, string note = null, int? aggregateCount = null)`

One traced call.

**Parameters**

- `when`: Wall-clock time of the call.
- `frame`: Unity frame counter.
- `realtime`: `Time.realtimeSinceStartup`.
- `gameClock`: The game's own clock, or null when it could not be read.
- `systemName`: Declaring namespace; null or empty becomes [`TraceLineBuilder.RootSystem`](#tracelinebuilder--rootsystem).
- `className`: Simple class name.
- `methodName`: Method name.
- `args`: Already-formatted arguments.
- `threadId`: Managed thread id the call ran on.
- `instance`: Already-formatted instance, or null for a static call.
- `returnValue`: Already-formatted return value; omitted when null.
- `note`: Free-text note, e.g. the suppression count; omitted when null.
- `aggregateCount`: When set, this line stands for a whole window of a polling method: it is written as `"agg":true,"count":N` and its arguments are the last ones seen in that window.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--footer"></a>

### `string Footer(DateTimeOffset when, int frame, double realtime, long lines, long suppressed, IReadOnlyList<string> pollingMethods = null, long busEmitted = 0, long busDropped = 0, IReadOnlyList<string> unpatchedMethods = null, TraceHealth cost = null)`

Last line of every file, written on `Application.quitting`. Carries the list of methods that were being aggregated, so a reader knows which counts are merged.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--header"></a>

### `string Header(DateTimeOffset when, TraceLevel level, int patched, int failed, int classes, double milliseconds)`

First line of every file: what was patched and how long it took, so a trace that looks empty can be told apart from a trace whose patching silently failed.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--health"></a>

### `string Health(TraceHealth health)`

Renders the health section of a snapshot, or `null` when there is none.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--snapshot"></a>

### `string Snapshot(TraceSnapshot snapshot)`

One periodic state snapshot.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--snapshotsummary"></a>

### `string SnapshotSummary(TraceSnapshot snapshot)`

The same snapshot as one compact console line, so the user can watch LogOutput.log with `tail -f` instead of reading JSON.

<a id="tracelinebuilder--ui"></a>

### `string Ui(DateTimeOffset when, int frame, double realtime, string gameClock, string controlType, string eventName, string path, string label, string value, int threadId, string source = null, int? aggregateCount = null)`

One user-interface event, from the Unity control layer rather than from a game class. Deliberately a shape of its own: what identifies a UGUI control is its hierarchy path and its label, not an argument list.

**Parameters**

- `controlType`: Control class, e.g. `Button` or `TMP_InputField`.
- `eventName`: What happened, e.g. `press`, `valueChanged`.
- `path`: Hierarchy path from [`UiPath`](#uipath).
- `label`: The control's visible text, when it has any.
- `value`: The new value, already formatted; omitted when null.
- `threadId`: Managed thread id the callback ran on.
- `source`: [`InteractionSource.User`](#interactionsource--user) or [`InteractionSource.Code`](#interactionsource--code) for a value change UGUI cannot attribute by itself; omitted when the event is unambiguous.
- `aggregateCount`: When set, this line stands for a window of a code-driven control: written as `"agg":true,"count":N`, exactly as for a polling game method.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy"></a>

## `TraceRetentionPolicy`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.TraceRetentionPolicy` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A2 trace retention, as pure decisions over a file listing. Archive-first: step 1 gzips every part of every past session; step 2, only if the folder is still over the cap, deletes whole past sessions, oldest first, always keeping the newest [`TraceRetentionPolicy.MinSessions`](#traceretentionpolicy--minsessions).

"Past" means a stamp that sorts before the current session's. The current session - and anything stamped later, which could only be another running instance or a clock that went backwards - is never compressed and never deleted. Its size still counts toward the cap, because it is on the disk. [`TraceRetentionRunner`](#traceretentionrunner) does the IO.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy--ctor"></a>

### `TraceRetentionPolicy(long maxTotalBytes, int minSessions, bool compressClosedParts)`

Creates a policy.

**Parameters**

- `maxTotalBytes`: Folder cap in bytes; 0 or less turns step 2 off.
- `minSessions`: Newest past sessions step 2 never deletes; negative means 0.
- `compressClosedParts`: Whether step 1 runs.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy--bytespermb"></a>

### `const long BytesPerMB = 1048576`

Bytes in one configured megabyte.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy--compressclosedparts"></a>

### `bool CompressClosedParts { get; }`

Whether past parts are archived.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy--maxtotalbytes"></a>

### `long MaxTotalBytes { get; }`

Folder cap in bytes; 0 = no cap.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy--minsessions"></a>

### `int MinSessions { get; }`

Newest past sessions that are never deleted.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy--fromconfig"></a>

### `static TraceRetentionPolicy FromConfig(TraceConfig config)`

The policy the `[Trace]` config asks for.

**Parameters**

- `config`: The bound trace configuration.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `config` is null.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy--plancompression"></a>

### `TraceCompressionPlan PlanCompression(IEnumerable<TraceFile> files, string currentStamp)`

Step 1: every plain part of every past session, plus interrupted archives to clear.

**Parameters**

- `files`: A folder listing.
- `currentStamp`: The live session's stamp.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `files` is null.
- `ArgumentException`: `currentStamp` is not a valid stamp.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy--plandeletion"></a>

### `TraceDeletionPlan PlanDeletion(IEnumerable<TraceFile> files, string currentStamp)`

Step 2: whole past sessions to delete, oldest first, until the folder fits the cap.

**Parameters**

- `files`: A folder listing, taken after step 1.
- `currentStamp`: The live session's stamp.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `files` is null.
- `ArgumentException`: `currentStamp` is not a valid stamp.

<a id="traceretentionpolicy--sessions"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<TraceSession> Sessions(IEnumerable<TraceFile> files)`

Groups the recognised files by session stamp, oldest session first, parts in order.

<a id="traceretentionrunner"></a>

## `TraceRetentionRunner`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.TraceRetentionRunner` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The thin IO half of [`TraceRetentionPolicy`](#traceretentionpolicy): lists the folder, runs step 1 one file at a time, lists again, runs step 2. Blocking and slow on purpose - run it on a background thread, never on Unity's main thread.

Never throws for a single file: every failure becomes a [`TraceRetentionAction.CompressFailed`](#traceretentionaction--compressfailed) or [`TraceRetentionAction.DeleteFailed`](#traceretentionaction--deletefailed) step, counted in [`TraceRetentionReport.Failures`](#traceretentionreport--failures), and the pass moves on.

<a id="traceretentionrunner--ctor"></a>

### `TraceRetentionRunner(string directory, string currentStamp, TraceRetentionPolicy policy, Action<TraceRetentionStep> onStep)`

Creates a runner for one folder and one live session.

**Parameters**

- `directory`: The trace folder.
- `currentStamp`: The live session's stamp; its files are never touched.
- `policy`: What to keep.
- `onStep`: Receives every per-file result as it happens. Required: it is where failures are logged.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: An argument is null.
- `ArgumentException`: `currentStamp` is not a valid stamp.

<a id="traceretentionrunner--list"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<TraceFile> List(string directory)`

Lists the recognised trace files in a folder (top level only), with their sizes.

**Parameters**

- `directory`: The trace folder.

**Returns:** The files; empty when the folder does not exist.

<a id="traceretentionrunner--run"></a>

### `TraceRetentionReport Run(CancellationToken cancel)`

Runs one pass: archive past parts, then delete oldest sessions while over the cap.

**Parameters**

- `cancel`: Checked between files and between buffers; set it when the game quits.

**Returns:** What was done.

## `TraceToggle`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.TraceToggle` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

RP-1: the diagnostic trace is off unless a player turns it on, and turning it on or off is one short command. The trace patches the game at startup, so `on` and `full` start at the next launch; `off` also stops a running trace at once (its hooks stay in place but write nothing).

<a id="tracetoggle--folder"></a>

### `const string Folder = "BepInEx/trace"`

Where the trace files go, relative to the game folder.

<a id="tracetoggle--usage"></a>

### `const string Usage = "trace on|off|full|status"`

The console usage line (also the Tab completions).

<a id="tracetoggle--name"></a>

### `static string Name(TraceLevel level)`

A short name for a level, as players see it.

<a id="tracetoggle--plan"></a>

### `static TraceTogglePlan Plan(IReadOnlyList<string> args, TraceLevel saved, TraceLevel running)`

Decides what `trace <args>` does.

**Parameters**

- `args`: The words after `trace`.
- `saved`: The level in the config file (what the next launch uses).
- `running`: What this session is recording: Off when the trace never started or was stopped.

<a id="uiownership"></a>

## `UiOwnership`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.UiOwnership` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Which Unity UI controls belong to the framework itself, so the trace's UI layer leaves them out: our own console and mod windows must never produce `TYPED`, `BUTTON` or `CLICK` lines (the Esc that closes the game-style console used to write `TYPED ""`).

**The rule.** A control is the framework's own when the root GameObject of its hierarchy (`Transform.root`) has a name that starts with [`UiOwnership.FrameworkRootPrefix`](#uiownership--frameworkrootprefix), compared ordinally and case-sensitively. Every object the framework creates at the top of a hierarchy uses that prefix: the game-style overlay canvas every game-style window lives on is `CWY.GameStyleCanvas` (`CwyLs.ModLoader.Bulbul/UI/GameStyleCanvas.cs`), and the hosts are `CWY.TraceHost`, `CWY.ConsoleHost` and so on.

The trace plugin cannot reference the adapter's types, so it matches by name, which is the one thing both sides can see. A control the framework adds under one of the game's own canvases (for example the language selector's extra entry) keeps the game's root and is traced like any game control. Anything that creates a new root for framework UI must keep the prefix.

<a id="uiownership--frameworkrootprefix"></a>

### `const string FrameworkRootPrefix = "CWY."`

The name prefix reserved for the framework's own root GameObjects.

<a id="uiownership--isframeworkroot"></a>

### `static bool IsFrameworkRoot(string rootName)`

True when a hierarchy whose root has this name belongs to the framework.

**Parameters**

- `rootName`: Name of the root GameObject; null or empty is never the framework's.

<a id="uipath"></a>

## `UiPath`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Trace.UiPath` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Builds the `Canvas/RoomUI/SettingButton` path that identifies a control in the scene. The walk itself belongs to the plugin (it needs `Transform`); the joining and capping live here so the rule is one testable function rather than a loop inside a Harmony prefix.

<a id="uipath--elision"></a>

### `const string Elision = "…"`

Marks a path whose root end was cut.

<a id="uipath--maxsegments"></a>

### `const int MaxSegments = 12`

Longest path written. Deep UGUI hierarchies are mostly layout wrappers.

<a id="uipath--build"></a>

### `static string Build(IReadOnlyList<string> namesRootFirst)`

Joins hierarchy names with '/'. Names must be ordered root first; when there are more than [`UiPath.MaxSegments`](#uipath--maxsegments), the segments nearest the control are kept, because those are the ones that identify it.
